findings.claim: A grid-exact beat rules out live-band rock of the 1960s and 1970s.
findings.truth: Exact timing can suggest a drum machine or programming, but cannot date a recording by itself. Drum machines were in use in late-1960s and 1970s popular and rock recordings.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Drum machine: 1960s rhythm machines; a 1969 hit, a 1971 number-one single and a 1972 Pink Floyd recording used drum machines. Spec 3.1.4 includes rock of the 1960s and 1970s.

findings.claim: The Queen tracks have equal weight and the set versions are the 2011 remasters.
findings.truth: The specification names three Queen tracks but does not state equal weighting or prescribe a 2011 remaster. It calls the middle track ‘The Seven Seas of Rhye’, while the fetched song source titles it ‘Seven Seas of Rhye’. Either retain the official recording title and remove the unsupported exam claims, or obtain a current official AQA study guide before standardising all references.

summary: All four lessons were read independently. One historical dating claim is corrected; practice-answer allocations are converted to unscored indicative answers, and the Queen recording/version issue needs an authoritative AQA source.
